mechanism_narrative: The sharp week-on-week collapse in WORKPLACES indicates fewer in-person trips that suppress adjacent shopping and dining visits, so RETAIL_REC should fall over the next four weeks relative to the prior four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -8.3 at t-1w to -37.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC averages above its previous 28-day mean despite WORKPLACES remaining below its t-1w level for two or more consecutive weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above its recent range, more time spent at home substitutes for discretionary outings and retail visits, pushing RETAIL_REC down within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds 15 points above baseline for at least one weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has been elevated in all four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays at or above 15 while RETAIL_REC rises relative to the prior 28-day mean over the next two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS combined with weaker TRANSIT signals a shift toward local outdoor activity rather than city-center shopping trips, which depresses RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -17.4 at t-1w to -9.4 at t-0w while TRANSIT dropped from -21.9 to -29.4
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to improve while TRANSIT remains depressed yet RETAIL_REC does not fall below its prior 28-day mean within four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden deterioration in TRANSIT beyond a 25-point deficit signals a new access constraint or service disruption that quickly reduces discretionary retail trips, lowering RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -25 on the weekly mean
failure_condition: If TRANSIT is below -25 and RETAIL_REC does not decline further in the following week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated GROCERY_PHARM indicates consolidated essential trips that can displace nonessential shopping visits; when this series stays positive for several weeks, RETAIL_REC should underperform over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -1.1 to 9.7 between t-3w and t-1w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains above zero for four weeks but RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 28-day mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES collapses while RESIDENTIAL rises, people reallocate time to home-based activity and cut discretionary errands; that joint shift predicts a retail decline over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -37.0 at t-0w while RESIDENTIAL rose to 16.7
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains sharply negative and RESIDENTIAL remains elevated yet RETAIL_REC does not fall within two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in PARKS over multiple weeks captures weather- or season-driven outdoor substitution that diverts spending from indoor retail and recreation, causing RETAIL_REC to weaken over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by at least 8 points from its prior weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -17.4 at t-1w to -9.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS improves by 8 or more points and RETAIL_REC still rises over the next month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals renewed mobility suppression that filters into retail demand after a short lag, so RETAIL_REC should be lower within one to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -25 and WORKPLACES falls below -30 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -29.4 and WORKPLACES was -37.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are below the stated thresholds but RETAIL_REC does not decline below its prior 28-day mean within one week, the hypothesis is rejected.
